title: Single instance lock and extra windows
when: Opening the app twice corrupts shared data, or the user wants a second window such as a preview or a detached panel.
inputs: should a second launch focus the first one
prompt:
Goal: Only one process owns the data folder, a second launch hands its file argument to the first and exits, and extra windows open through the window API.
Steps:
1. On start write app.lock in the data folder with { pid: NL_PID, port: NL_PORT, t: Date.now() } and refresh t every 10 seconds.
2. If app.lock exists with t newer than 30 seconds, another instance runs: write the file path from NL_ARGS into inbox.json, then Neutralino.app.exit().
3. The running instance polls inbox.json every 2 seconds (or uses Neutralino.filesystem.createWatcher where available), opens the file, deletes the inbox and calls Neutralino.window.focus().
4. Remove app.lock on windowClose; a stale lock older than 30 seconds is taken over.
5. Extra window: Neutralino.window.create("/preview.html", { width: 600, height: 800, title: "Preview" }); it runs as its own process, so share data through files or the extension bridge, not memory.
6. Give each window one job; the main window owns writes, others only read.
7. Allow window.create, window.focus and the needed filesystem calls only.
Quality bar:
- Double clicking a document never opens two writers.
- A crash does not block the next start forever.
Pitfalls:
- Lock files without a heartbeat, which stay stale after a crash.
- Two windows writing the same JSON file.
Verify:
- [ ] Lock has a timestamp and stale check.
- [ ] Second launch forwards arguments and exits.
- [ ] Only the main window writes data.
Output: instance.js, preview.html and allow list lines.

examples.input: se abro o app duas vezes os dados se perdem
examples.output: app.lock with heartbeat, second launch forwards path via inbox.json and exits, preview via window.create
